title: Separate child and adolescent mental health facilities (Kenya Mental Health Policy 2015-2030)
description_to_check: The national mental health policy lists, among its priority actions, the establishment of separate outpatient and inpatient facilities for children and adolescents. It also sets a life-course principle: mental health policies, plans and services must account for needs from infancy through adolescence.
source_name: Kenya Mental Health Policy 2015-2030 (Ministry of Health), Section 2.3.8 Infrastructure, Priority Actions; Section 2.3.10 Vulnerable groups

title: Safeguards for children admitted to mental health facilities (National Mental Health Act)
description_to_check: The National Mental Health Act sets conditions for admitting a child to a mental health facility. Section 39(1) allows admission only where the child's living area is separate from adult patients and the Federal Ministry of Health or a state agency has inspected and certified in writing that treatment will be in the least restrictive environment, with facilities that meet the child's developmental needs. Involuntary admission or detention of a child is a last resort, only where community-based alternatives are unavailable, unlikely to be effective or have failed. Another provision requires mental health to be integrated into disease-specific programmes, including adolescent health programmes.
source_name: National Mental Health Act, 2021 (Act No. 46), Nigeria, Section 39(1) and the proviso on involuntary admission of a child; published in Official Gazette No. 229, Vol. 109, Lagos, 30 December 2022

title: Child and adolescent mental health services in the district system and in hospital units (National Mental Health Policy Framework 2023-2030)
description_to_check: The national mental health policy framework and strategic plan for 2023 to 2030 commits to strengthening the district mental health system, including detection and management of child and adolescent mental disorders in primary health care clinics and at community level such as schools, with referral where appropriate. Its infrastructure objective requires mental health units attached to regional and tertiary hospitals to have facilities for child and adolescent inpatient care, with a 2030 completion date, led by the National Department of Health and provincial departments of health. It also lists strengthening child and adolescent services as a priority area.
source_name: National Mental Health Policy Framework and Strategic Plan 2023-2030 (Department of Health), Section 1

title: Suicide prevention with attention to youth (Mental Health Act, Republic Act 11036)
description_to_check: The Mental Health Act declares the right of all Filipinos to mental health. Section 21 requires mental health services to include suicide prevention and response, with particular attention to youth, and requires 24/7 hotlines to be set up and existing ones strengthened.

title: Right to mental health prioritising children, adolescents and young people (Ley 2460 de 2025)
description_to_check: Ley 2460 of 2025 amends the mental health law (Ley 1616 of 2013). Its purpose is to guarantee the full exercise of the right to mental health, prioritising children, adolescents and young people, through health promotion, prevention of mental disorders and integrated care. It requires emotional education and comprehensive care for children and young people, priority mental health care for ages 14 to 28 without prejudice to the priority given to children and adolescents, and, within one year, a protocol for the promotion and care of mental health and prevention of mental disorders for children, adolescents and young people. It also requires mental health committees linking health and education institutions.
source_name: Ley 2460 de 2025 (16 June 2025), Articulo 3 (amended Articulo 1 of Ley 1616 de 2013), Articulos 19 and 25; Official Gazette 53153 of 18 June 2025

title: Child and adolescent mental health services in primary care (National Mental Health Policy 2011-2021)
description_to_check: The national mental health policy (January 2011) supports integrating mental health services into primary health care under WHO's mhGAP programme. At primary care level, services will be provided to adults, children and adolescents, covering early detection and diagnosis, basic psychosocial interventions, pharmacological treatment, referral and follow-up. The policy starts with depression, unexplained somatic complaints and developmental disorders, delivered by specially trained family doctors, general practitioners and nurses. A 2023 country report notes that Jordan has no mental health act and no legislation specific to children, adolescents or new mothers.

title: Mental Health Support Teams to reach national coverage in schools and colleges, England (10 Year Health Plan, 2025)
description_to_check: The government's 10 Year Health Plan for England (July 2025) says it will continue to roll out Mental Health Support Teams in schools and colleges to reach full national coverage by 2029 to 2030, and will embed mental health support for children and young people in new Young Futures Hubs. The plan also commits to recruiting 8,500 mental health staff across children's and adult services. A June 2026 government release reports almost 11,800 schools and colleges now served, nearly 80% of secondary schools with access, and the 8,500 recruitment achieved. Applies to England only.
source_name: Department of Health and Social Care and Prime Minister's Office (2025, July; updated 30 July 2025), Fit for the future: 10 Year Health Plan for England (accessible version), GOV.UK, Chapter 4 'Thriving young lives'

title: School counsellors and adolescent mental health services (National Plan of Action for Adolescent Health 2017-2030)
description_to_check: The National Plan of Action for Adolescent Health 2017-2030 sets measurable actions on adolescent mental health. They include training for all primary health care workers on adolescent mental health (target 100%), a standard assessment tool for mental health problems, referral of identified cases by field workers (target 100%), a psychiatrist in all district hospitals and a psychologist in all districts and upazilas, a counsellor in all schools and colleges (led by the Ministry of Education), and referral links between schools, adolescent clubs, communities and health facilities. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare leads most actions, with time frames across 2018 to 2030.
source_name: National Plan of Action for Adolescent Health Strategy 2017-2030 (MCH Services Unit, Directorate General of Family Planning, with UNICEF, UNFPA and WHO), mental health actions table, printed pages 37 and 38 (PDF pages 35 and 36)
